almanac.reason: Cool slate mid-tone stock, Hanken Grotesk over Newsreader with mono figures, chart magenta; no catalog style is a reference-book material.

arcade.reason: Same arcade-game family. Arcade is an aubergine CRT ground with RGB-split Bungee, Silkscreen figures, hard offset shadows and ember/acid inks; pacman is black with Press Start 2P and blue, sega white with VT323 and rainbow offset blocks, tetris pale blue with Bangers.

atelier.reason: Both are quiet, restrained serif-led light pages. Atelier is limewash paper, umber ink, Sentient light over Hanken Grotesk, cotton card stock and a slate signal; refined is white with Playfair Display and generic blue/violet tokens.

bloom.reason: Warm grained off-white with a generated working grid, terracotta blooms, Ranade and rubber cased parts lit from above; no catalog style uses this moulded-part material.

blueprint.reason: Prussian-blue mid-tone sheet with white line ink, Chakra Petch, dimension strings and cyanotype photographs; no catalog style is a technical drawing material.

broadside.reason: Both are loud heavy-capital poster registers. Broadside is grained buff stock, Six Caps and Bevan wood capitals, one- and five-point rules and one vermilion; bold is a near-black surface with Archivo Black and blue/green tokens.

brutal.reason: Same brutalist tradition, different material: brutal is near-white stock, black 3px drawn cells, uppercase Libre Franklin 900, zero radius and one acid-yellow fill with no offset shadows; brutalism is orange-red concrete with Darker Grotesque, neobrutalism a warm surface with Inter, yellow plus violet and 4/8px radius.

carnival.reason: Same loud full-colour family. Carnival is screen-printed tinted paper, Big Shoulders Display capitals, a hard 4px ink shadow and two competing accent fields; vibrant is white with Fascinate and purple/peach, expressive white with pink/blue and IBM Plex Mono.

cobalt.reason: Both are light, restrained developer-tool registers in a grotesk. Cobalt adds cool near-white paper, Familjen Grotesk over IBM Plex Sans, an ASCII field, keycap buttons, cut-corner panels and an electric cobalt signal; shadcn is a monochrome Geist utility system.

console.reason: Graphite dark ground in three steps, Host Grotesk with Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for measured values, amber for people and blue for instruments; no catalog style matches.

coral.reason: Read beside style:clean and style:professional: those are generic white SaaS tokens (blue/violet Poppins, yellow/black). Coral is warm grey paper on a felt desk, cotton stationery, letterpress card controls and a coral press, so no material is shared.

darkroom.reason: Warm print-black ground with fine grain, fibre-white ink, hairline Sofia Sans Extra Condensed and one amber safelight; no catalog style is a photographic darkroom material.

dose.reason: Warm morning paper, translucent tinted plastic, moulded controls, DM Mono pharmacy labels and pharmacy green; no catalog style uses this material.

dusk.reason: Both are dark cool grotesk pages with glass panels. Dusk is slate under a real dusk landscape, smoked glass with a lit edge, Wix Madefor, bone wells and periwinkle plus apricot; enterprise is a near-black IBM Plex Sans data dashboard with one blue.

editorial.reason: Same name and magazine tradition, different material: the theme is warm white uncoated stock, Bricolage Grotesque condensed 800 over Source Serif 4, a heavy ink rule and one printer's green; the style is black/white with Gelasio serif heads.

formwork.reason: Warm grey concrete paper with speck grain, Oswald capitals, square cast edges, hard shadows and safety orange; the brutalism style shares the concrete idea but not this mid-tone stock, face or signal.

furrow.reason: Warm manila paper, generated survey-map contours in sienna and slate, Red Hat Display and moulded keys; no catalog style is a field-survey material.

garden.reason: Warm oat paper, deep green ink, Vollkorn with old-style figures over Hanken Grotesk, moss and clay tints, one leaf green; no catalog style matches.

grid.reason: Both are structured light grotesk systems. Grid is Swiss style proper: white poster stock, Radio Canada Big, flat ultramarine fields and one Swiss red, no strokes; geometric is a generic Inter system with blue/violet tokens.

halftone.reason: Both build tone from dot patterns. Halftone is butter-cream stock, brown-black ink, an Ultra slab and one vermilion printed solid and as a dot screen; dithered is a generic dither technique on white with mono type.

hedgerow.reason: Deep leaf-green dark paper, cream ink, Prata over Manrope, pill controls and a chartreuse signal; no catalog style matches.

hum.reason: Same approachable rounded family. Hum is grained cream cut paper with torn edges, pressable card stock, Chillax and three unblended accents; friendly is soft pastel with Noto Serif Display, lingo bright green Nunito with 3D borders.

ink.reason: White paper, a black with no hue, Epilogue 700 over 400, hairline rules and state pills, one teal; no catalog style uses a zero-chroma notice-board material.

kiln.reason: Near-black ground, cream ink, Boska over Geist, smoked wells, a heat ramp and an ember signal; no catalog style matches.

loom.reason: Ecru paper with sand steps, Libre Caslon Display over Hanken Grotesk, cloth photographed in window light, one deep indigo; no catalog style matches.

lumen.reason: Violet-black ground, lowercase Instrument Serif, Geist Mono, a faint blueprint grid, molten brass and a rose verb; no catalog style matches.

manifesto.reason: Same dark high-contrast display family. Manifesto is a warm near-black sheet, Anton capitals at poster size over Public Sans, a heavy ink bar and one fighting red; power is black monochrome with Oswald, dramatic near-black with violet and rose.

midnight.reason: Midnight-blue ground to every edge, Mona Sans expanded at 300, square-cut surfaces in lightness steps and an azure signal; no catalog style matches.

newsprint.reason: Same print-on-paper family. Newsprint is pale newsprint stock, warm black, Zilla Slab over Spectral with Franklin agate, column rules, a double rule and dried brick; paper is white with Montserrat, basic white with Oswald and violet.

overprint.reason: Grey newsprint stock, wide heavy Anybody capitals and teal plus orange passes that multiply to moss; the riso style uses pink and blue drums, so the inks and stock differ.

pasteup.reason: Kraft board with a fibre wash, League Gothic over a Newsreader galley, copy-paper lifts and one fluorescent yellow sheet; no catalog style matches.

piste.reason: Snow-white paper, cold near-black, Barlow Condensed 800 caps on 2px ink rules and one cobalt field; no catalog style matches.

refract.reason: Same light and clear-surface family, but refract rejects frosted blur: sunlit white plaster, live caustics or prism light, pool-blue ink, Funnel Display light and tinted cast shadows; glassmorphism and airy-glass are blurred frosted panels.

ribbon.reason: Warm off-white or blue-black night, Instrument Sans over Figtree, machined parts lit from above and the hour drawn as light; no catalog style matches.

rim.reason: Warm black paper, Switzer 500 with Geist Mono measurements, square hairline surfaces, earth photographed straight down, orange plus sky blue; no catalog style matches.

riso.reason: Same material read side by side: warm off-white paper, blue drum for type and structure, fluorescent pink as the only fill, a grotesk display and print offset. The theme carries real OKLCH drums, Cabinet Grotesk over Literata, grain and overprint rules, so it replaces the thinner style entry.

solstice.reason: Both are cream paper, brown ink, a fat display serif and one warm signal. Solstice adds gold hairlines, hard paper shadows, Yeseva One over Archivo Narrow and vermilion, and rejects the terracotta-on-cream template that the terracotta style is.

specimen.reason: Warm oat paper, razor-hairline Bodoni Moda over Geist, square 1px rules, one ink blue that draws metric guides; no catalog style matches.

spore.reason: Coffee-ground black with warm grain, parchment ink, Young Serif, grained wells and oyster pink; no catalog style matches.

sport.reason: Cool concrete paper, uppercase Saira Condensed over Albert Sans, mono times and one volt fill; no catalog style matches.

squeeze.reason: Forest-green mid-tone paper with real chroma, Gabarito 800, rounded tiles and peach controls; no catalog style matches.

sticker.reason: Warm off-white paper, Bowlby One SC, white die-cut borders on hard offset shadows, hot pink and lime fills; neobrutalism shares offset depth but not die-cut edges or these inks.

studio.reason: Cool proof paper with an ink dot grid and grain, Hedvig Letters Serif over Geist, crop marks and orange construction guides; no catalog style matches.

terminal.reason: Read side by side: matrix shares a dark ground, all-mono type and one green, but is a flat order-book surface in Space Mono with 2px corners; mono is a light stone surface. Terminal is a green-cast three-step ground, Martian Mono wide and narrow, and pictures printed as character grids, so it clusters instead of replacing.

terrazzo.reason: Off-white paper, white card surfaces ruled in ink over a hard offset, wide Syne over Onest, rust signal; no catalog style matches.

ultraviolet.reason: Read beside style:neon: neon is lime and cyan glow on white with Roboto. Ultraviolet is lavender paper in one violet pigment, lowercase Outfit, hairline pills, and rejects neon flyers, so no material is shared.

vantage.reason: Blue-black ground, a live point cloud lit by a sweep, Geologica light with sharpened corners and corner-tick frames; no catalog style matches.

vellum.reason: Parchment paper with a tan fibre wash, Grenze Gotisch blackletter heads, double rules and one ultramarine; no catalog style matches.

wayfind.reason: Cool grey paper, Chivo Mono throughout, square 2px ink borders and ink plates, cobalt for live and amber for figures; a light signage material unlike the dark mono styles.

werkstatt.reason: Warm putty mid-tone ground, Jost 700 capitals over Karla, 2px and 3px boxed cells, flat ultramarine, vermilion and yellow primaries; no catalog style matches.
